domain_label: Sweater Vertical Manufacturing Economics — Make-vs-Buy at Capsule Scale
purpose: A session-bounded method for a small AI-designed D2C knitwear brand sourcing in Ludhiana and selling in California/Turlock to decide the make-vs-buy boundary at capsule scale across the stage ladder (spinning=buy, dyeing=never own, knitting=subcontract-then-used-at-volume, linking=subcontract-last, finishing=subcontract, design+brand+US-import=OWN), to choose among the three real 'buy' implementations the consensus collapsed (B1 multi-job-worker mesh, B2 single-vertical full-package FOB, B3 greige+controlled-dye), to weigh the honest counters (QC fragmentation across micro-vendors, no captive-margin cushion, micro-volume fixed-cost penalty, supplier-power at tiny orders) and analyst-B's alternatives and flip-conditions, and to recompute the buy-vs-own-knitting utilisation breakeven on the [UNKNOWN] Ludhiana per-piece job-work rate — reaching buy-at-launch as a TESTED conclusion with explicit flip-conditions, never an asserted one, and never fabricating the missing rate.
assumptions: no live Ludhiana mandi, job-worker, or FOB-exporter quote is supplied; every cost, price, throughput, MOQ, and breakeven figure is a labeled [ESTIMATE] with method, basis, and confidence, or a named [UNKNOWN], never a fake-precise [FACT]

the venture is the small AI-designed D2C woollen/acrylic knitwear brand of the SCOPE_GLOSSARY scope statement, selling a 3-article capsule (A1 cotton-blend core, A2 fine-acrylic value, A3 merino/lambswool premium) into warm California/Turlock, low volume

this models the ex-factory conversion-cost boundary and the make-vs-buy decision on it, NOT landed cost, NOT COGS-to-stock, NOT a P&L; freight, US duty, CAC, and contribution margin are the T9/T7 survival test downstream

the make-vs-buy verdict is built from the T4 DEEPDIVE now CROSS-EXAMINED by the independent analyst-B memo, so the verdict is a tested A/B conclusion, not the reconstructed-consensus the DEEPDIVE flagged as un-challenged

the single highest-leverage missing number — the Ludhiana per-piece knit + LINK job-work rate — is held [UNKNOWN] and named as THE blocker; the FOB price + MOQ at a named vertical exporter is the twin [UNKNOWN] analyst-B adds; neither is fabricated
off-paper / friction costs are described as mechanism not accusation, every rupee amount [UNKNOWN] by design, and are episodic/cash-cycle costs named but never added as a clean per-garment COGS line
exclusions: landed cost (ocean freight, US duty cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% / wool 6110.11 ~16% / acrylic-MMF 6110.30.30 ~32%, insurance, broker, drayage, financing) — the T9 model
the D2C P&L survival test (CAC, returns, payment fees, AOV, LTV:CAC, contribution margin) — the T7/T9 decision that, not factory cost, governs viability
the yarn fibre/count/quality-spec decision and the dye-method call (T2 yarn specialist) beyond naming yarn as the cost-stack level-setter
the machine-acquisition price bands, throughput, and HSN 8447 import stack (T3 machines specialist) beyond consuming the buy-vs-own-knitting breakeven they feed

a committed bottom-up financial pro forma for an owned line (rebuilt against a real named Ludhiana unit downstream); this models the boundary decision and its breakeven structure, not the financial plan
any named-party accusation of bribery, evasion, or off-paper conduct; the off-paper layer is mechanism-only with [UNKNOWN] magnitudes

glossary.definition: The cost this model computes: full (dyed) yarn + knit job-work + LINK job-work + finishing + trims/labels/pack, plus EPF/ESI compliance loading on the labour-bearing portion and job-worker overhead/margin, ending at the factory gate. It is explicitly NOT landed cost, NOT COGS-to-stock, NOT a P&L, and NOT a live quote; it feeds FOB then the T9 landed stack.

The Ludhiana per-piece knit + LINK conversion charge (Rs/piece at 7GG/12GG for 300-400 g pullovers) — the single highest-value missing number, ~25-45% of the conversion subtotal, with no reliable public figure. It sets the uncertainty on every cost band AND decides the make-vs-buy crossover; held [UNKNOWN], named as THE blocker, never fabricated (carried from Ludhiana Open Q#1, Machines Open Q#2).

The structural fact that yarn sets the LEVEL of the cost stack and is well-anchored (~50-60% of the knit-garment stack; Vardhman FY20 raw material = 54% of revenue [FACT]; ~$1-2.50 of fibre per value/core sweater), while the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK per-piece rate sets the UNCERTAINTY — so the highest-leverage action is chasing the one rate, not cheaper yarn.

The 'buy' implementation where the brand buys bought-dyed yarn and subcontracts knit -> link -> finish across several micro-vendors within the Ludhiana agglomeration, coordinating the hand-offs itself; the brand owns QC across many seams, carries no captive-margin cushion, and gets the lowest MOQ (~100-300 pcs/style-colour). The only buy model the original consensus actually priced.

The 'buy' implementation where one integrated Ludhiana manufacturer-cum-exporter sources yarn and delivers finished, packed, export-cleared goods at an FOB price (GLOSSARY FPP). The vendor owns QC inside one firm (one throat to choke) and its captive-spinning margin can partly subsidise the buyer; it loses on higher MOQ (~300-1,000+ pcs/style [ESTIMATE], the number [UNKNOWN] at a named unit) and lost material/yarn control. The genuinely competitive option the consensus dismissed unpriced.

The 'buy' implementation where the brand buys greige yarn, controls one job-work dyer for one hero colour, and pays CMT for cut-make-trim-link (GLOSSARY CMT), keeping material + colour IP on a narrower surface. Direction concurs with consensus (never own the dyehouse) but its timing — pulling hero-colour dye control forward to launch — is more aggressive than the consensus's graduate-later.

The utilisation at which owning a knitting line just covers its fixed cost from the per-piece conversion saving over job-work: breakeven_utilisation = owned_fixed_period_cost / ((jobwork_unit_rate - owned_variable_unit_cost) * period_capacity). Below it subcontract wins; above it owning wins. It is controlled entirely by the [UNKNOWN] job-work rate, so the crossover cannot be located without that number.

The per-style fixed costs (sampling/PPS, tech-pack, lab dips, AQL inspection setup, ~$300-1,500/style [ESTIMATE, LOW]) amortised over a tiny MOQ, which push true micro-volume ex-factory cost MATERIALLY ABOVE the variable-only per-article bands — plausibly 1.3-2x the band midpoint over a 150-piece run; the most quantifiable buy-verdict fragility, and partly an argument FOR the higher-MOQ FOB option.

The internal factory margin a vertically-integrated firm can reallocate across captive stages to absorb a yarn-price spike, a bad season, or a returns wave. A buy-everything brand has zero captive margin to net against shocks; the honest mitigation is pricing the cushion into MSRP and holding cash, NOT owning a sub-scale stage whose captive margin is negative.

The asymmetric weakness of a micro-buyer placing 150-300 pc orders inside a job-worker's or exporter's book: worst per-piece price, lowest queue priority (especially in the Jul-Oct peak), and the B-team on QC. The compliant paper-clean posture the export brand must hold can itself be a queue penalty; mechanism not accusation, amounts [UNKNOWN]. B2 partly mitigates by making the brand a wanted account.

Owning a small sampling/finishing cell (used hand-flat ~$200-1,500, used linker ~$500-4,000, used press ~$1,000-8,000) plus a contracted programmer seat, to iterate prototypes in-house overnight then send only proven designs to the mesh/FOB for bulk. Justified on a SPEED/CONTROL axis (the brand's AI-design edge is bottlenecked by someone else's 2-5 wk sample queue), NOT on unit cost, so the utilisation argument against owning bulk does not apply.

nodes.definition: Pin down what this model computes and the four things it is NOT, because getting the boundary wrong is the most expensive mistake in the segment. It computes EX-FACTORY CONVERSION COST per garment: full (dyed) yarn + knit job-work + LINK job-work + finishing + trims/labels/pack -> direct-conversion subtotal, + EPF/ESI compliance loading (~15%+, on the on-roll labour portion only) + factory overhead / job-worker margin = ex-factory cost, which feeds FOB then the T9 landed stack. It is NOT landed cost (ocean freight, US duty cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% / wool 6110.11 ~16% / acrylic-MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% [FACT-USITC], insurance, broker, drayage, financing live in T9), NOT COGS-to-stock, NOT a P&L (CAC, returns, AOV, contribution margin are the T7/T9 viability test, and per the cross-team rule contribution margin after CAC not factory cost decides viability), and NOT a quote (bands only). The factory gate is the cheapest, least-decisive part of the journey; the discipline is to cost it honestly then hand the margin fight downstream.

nodes.definition: Lay down the make-vs-buy boundary stage by stage at capsule scale, the spine every downstream judgment hangs on. Spinning/yarn: BUY market yarn in-cluster, make never at this scale (integrated groups hold captive-spinning margin we cannot match; yarn is a commodity input we spec, not make). Dyeing: BUY bought-dyed stock shades, job-work dye only a proven hero colour, NEVER own (separate node — highest-regulatory-risk node). Knitting: SUBCONTRACT the FF panels, buy used (Cixing-class first) only when one style runs at proven sustained volume (separate breakeven node). Linking: SUBCONTRACT, in-source LAST (separate node — the throughput ceiling and hardest re-hire). Finishing: SUBCONTRACT (optionally one cheap used press for sampling). Design + brand + US import (importer of record): OWN, always (separate node — the venture's entire edge and where downstream margin is captured). Graduate toward owning a step only when one specific repeating program runs at proven sustained volume, linking last; never own a dyehouse, never build a machine.

nodes.definition: Establish the one part of the chain the venture must OWN: design + brand + US import (importer of record), always, at launch and after. This is the venture's entire edge and the only place downstream margin is captured — the same lesson the cluster's own winners learned (manufacture -> own-brand retail; T1). The brand owns the AI design pipeline, the brand and its D2C story, and the legal importer-of-record position that carries US duty/compliance liability and unlocks the clean-doc posture RoSCTL/RoDTEP refunds and US import require. Everything upstream of design is a buy/subcontract decision; everything at and downstream of design is owned. This is NOT a cost-minimisation choice — it is the strategic spine, and it is why over-optimising the factory gate is the wrong fight: the margin is captured here and in US D2C, not at the loom.

nodes.definition: Establish the absolute 'never own' at the dyeing stage, the highest-confidence make-vs-buy boundary in the segment. Dyeing is the highest-regulatory-risk node in the entire cluster: all three Ludhiana CETPs were found non-compliant, CPCB levied penalties worth crores, the NGT is reviewing the cluster, and closure exposure is wildly out of proportion to a 3-article line [FACT-enforcement; ESTIMATE: judgment, HIGH]. Owning a dyehouse is never on the table at any volume for this venture. The binding number either way is the dye-lot MOQ per shade (~150-500 kg/colour => 2-4 launch colours), not the dye method.

nodes.definition: Make the case for single-vertical full-package FOB (B2) as a genuinely competitive launch option the consensus dismissed unpriced, and where it loses. nodes.definition: Compute the buy-vs-own-knitting breakeven on utilisation as a recomputing labeled [ESTIMATE]. Formula: breakeven_utilisation = owned_fixed_period_cost / ((jobwork_unit_rate - owned_variable_unit_cost) * period_capacity). owned_fixed_period_cost is the per-period amortised landed machine cost plus the programmer seat, skilled payroll, and power/infrastructure; jobwork_unit_rate is the per-sweater knit+LINK conversion charge the mesh quotes (the [UNKNOWN] rate); owned_variable_unit_cost is in-house per-sweater yarn-handling, energy, and consumables; period_capacity is the linker-bound sweaters the owned line can ship per period. Worked illustration [ESTIMATE: arithmetic, LOW-MED, placeholder inputs because the rate is [UNKNOWN]]: owned_fixed_period_cost ~$7,500/mo, conversion saving (jobwork_unit_rate - owned_variable_unit_cost) ~$5/sweater, period_capacity ~800 sweaters/mo (linker-bound) -> breakeven_utilisation = 7500 / (5 * 800) = 7500 / 4000 = 1.875, i.e. ABOVE 100% — the line cannot break even at this saving and capacity, so subcontract wins until either the conversion saving rises or the fixed cost falls or capacity is genuinely filled. Below the breakeven utilisation subcontract wins; only one repeating program at sustained volume that fills the linker-bound capacity clears it. The whole computation is gated by the [UNKNOWN] job-work rate; recompute with a real rate and a landed machine quote before any cost model commits.

nodes.definition: Establish that the same garment has three different costs by volume and that the curve is the bridge into the T9 landed P&L. Micro (launch capsule, ~150-650 pcs/colour): HIGHEST per piece — the variable stack plus the small-batch dye surcharge (+20-50%/colour) plus per-style setup spread thin, so real cost sits ABOVE the per-article bands; posture: buy everything (subcontract knit/link/finish, bought-dyed yarn), high confidence. Small-batch repeat (a hero style/colour proven, low-thousands): FALLS toward the bands — setup amortises, dye lots hit economic MOQ (surcharge gone), job-workers give better repeat rates; posture: still buy, but begin pricing a used Cixing-class machine for the one repeating program. Sustained volume (one program filling a machine + linkers + a programmer): LOWEST per piece, but only if utilisation is genuinely full; owning knitting can beat subcontracting once a specific repeating program runs at proven sustained volume — the crossover the [UNKNOWN] job-work rate decides; posture: selectively make (knitting first, linking last), never dye, never build. Three scaling rules into T9: (1) volume cuts cost through two channels — amortising per-style setup AND clearing the dye-lot surcharge — both threshold effects, so cost drops in STEPS not smoothly, the first step being the ~500 kg/colour dye economic MOQ; (2) the make-vs-buy crossover IS the [UNKNOWN] rate, so volume strategy and the blocker are the same question; (3) ex-factory -> landed MULTIPLIES not adds — T9 stacks freight + duty (cotton ~16.5% ~ wool ~16%, with acrylic/MMF ~32% the outlier) + insurance + broker + drayage + financing, and duty is a percentage so it scales with the ex-factory level, which is why A3's premium fibre price compounds at landed and the acrylic A2 is the article most penalized at the border (32% MMF duty), while A1's cotton core stays the friendliest into the US on demand/sell-window/repeat-LTV grounds, not a duty edge over wool.

nodes.definition: Bind the honesty discipline into every claim, because the segment is honest-but-imprecise by exactly one input. Tag every money/capacity/performance/regulation claim [FACT] (cited public source / true-by-definition identity), [ESTIMATE] (method + basis + confidence, carrying the literal word estimate), or [UNKNOWN] (genuinely not known, named as a blocker, never fabricated); coverage is a floor not a ceiling. Cost/price/throughput/MOQ bands are [ESTIMATE], never fake-precise. The genuinely-missing numbers stay [UNKNOWN] and are named as blockers: the Ludhiana per-piece knit + LINK job-work rate (THE blocker) and the all-in FOB price + MOQ at a named single-vertical exporter (the twin blocker). No over-promising: no magic device, no build-our-own-machine, AI is a multiplier not a substitute. The off-paper / friction economy is described as MECHANISM not accusation — no named person or firm is alleged to do anything, every rupee amount is [UNKNOWN] by design — and it is an episodic/cash-cycle cost named but never added as a clean per-garment COGS line. The ~15%+ EPF/ESI compliance loading is applied only to the labour-bearing portion of conversion the brand carries on its own roll, with the competitor-gap magnitude [UNKNOWN]. This discipline is what makes the verdict trustworthy: a tested conclusion, not an asserted one.

dominance_rules.rule: The ex-factory boundary dominates any viability claim
dominance_rules.rationale: a great ex-factory number is not viability; contribution margin after CAC decides survival, so the gate must never be read as the P&L
dominance_rules.trigger: an ex-factory band is treated as landed cost or as proof of viability
dominance_rules.action: restate the boundary and hand the margin fight to T9/T7 before drawing a viability conclusion

dominance_rules.rule: Holding the [UNKNOWN] job-work rate dominates any decidable-looking breakeven
dominance_rules.rationale: fabricating the rate to make the breakeven decidable contaminates every band and the crossover
dominance_rules.trigger: a per-piece rate is invented or hardened from trade lore
dominance_rules.action: hold the rate [UNKNOWN], keep the breakeven an illustration, and run the quote run

dominance_rules.rule: Never owning a dyehouse dominates any colour-control gain
dominance_rules.rationale: the crore-scale CETP/NGT closure exposure is wildly out of proportion to a 3-article line
dominance_rules.trigger: an owned dyehouse is considered to gain colour control
dominance_rules.action: keep dye outsourced (bought-dyed or one controlled job-work dyer), never owned

dominance_rules.rationale: ~$2M-10M over years for a likely-inferior result versus a sub-$20k working used machine is a catastrophic misallocation
dominance_rules.trigger: a build-your-own-machine project is floated, including on an AI premise
dominance_rules.action: kill the build option and keep AI to the program/maintenance/QC software layers

dominance_rules.rule: Choosing among B1/B2/B3 on evidence dominates defaulting into the mesh
dominance_rules.rationale: the consensus priced only B1 and dismissed the option (B2) that fixes its own admitted fragilities
dominance_rules.trigger: a buy decision is about to default into the multi-vendor mesh unexamined
dominance_rules.action: run the B1-vs-B2 trade study on the quote run before committing

dominance_rules.rule: The real first cheque dominates the unit cost when sizing the launch
dominance_rules.rationale: dye-lot MOQ + per-style setup + months of tied-up cash, not unit-cost x pieces, is what bankrupts a profitable-looking brand
dominance_rules.trigger: the launch is sized on unit cost
dominance_rules.action: size it on the dye-lot MOQ (2-4 colours) + setup + cash-out and don't launch into the Jul-Oct peak

dominance_rules.rule: Own-for-speed dominates own-for-unit-cost only on the sampling loop
dominance_rules.rationale: the sampling cell is justified on speed/control where the bulk utilisation breakeven does not apply, and nowhere else
dominance_rules.trigger: a sampling cell is judged on unit cost or an owned bulk line is justified on speed
dominance_rules.action: own only the sampling loop on speed and keep bulk subcontracted on the unit-cost breakeven

dominance_rules.rule: Linking owned LAST dominates any quality-driven early in-sourcing
dominance_rules.rationale: the linker is the throughput ceiling and the hardest re-hire, so owning it early imports the bottleneck and staffing risk
dominance_rules.trigger: linking is considered for in-sourcing before knitting or at launch
dominance_rules.action: own linking strictly after knitting clears the breakeven and only with lean-season-staffable linkers

dominance_rules.rule: Mechanism-not-accusation dominates any off-paper cost claim
dominance_rules.rationale: the off-paper layer is a structural incentive, not a named-party act, and its amounts are [UNKNOWN] by design
dominance_rules.trigger: an off-paper or friction cost is about to be added as a per-garment COGS line or pinned on a party
dominance_rules.action: describe it as mechanism with [UNKNOWN] amounts and keep it out of the per-garment stack

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the ex-factory boundary before quoting any cost number
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an ex-factory band being mistaken for landed cost or a P&L and the launch mis-sized

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold the knit+LINK rate and FOB MOQ [UNKNOWN] before building any breakeven or first-cheque figure
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a fabricated rate contaminating every band, the crossover, and the launch cheque

anti_rework_rules.rule: Split 'buy' into B1/B2/B3 before committing a buy decision
anti_rework_rules.prevents: defaulting into the mesh and re-sourcing after the dismissed B2 option turns out to win

anti_rework_rules.rule: Uplift the variable bands by the per-style setup and dye surcharge before any micro-volume margin use
anti_rework_rules.prevents: quoting setup-free bands as true micro-volume cost and under-pricing the launch

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compute the utilisation breakeven before considering owning any knitting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: buying iron before a program can fill it and the breakeven clears

anti_rework_rules.rule: Own linking only after knitting and only with lean-season-staffable linkers
anti_rework_rules.prevents: importing the throughput bottleneck and hardest-to-hire skill at the wrong time

anti_rework_rules.rule: Justify the sampling cell on speed, never on unit cost, before owning it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: dismissing a worthwhile speed investment on the wrong axis or owning bulk on a speed pretext

anti_rework_rules.rule: Schedule the launch drop out of the Jul-Oct peak before committing yarn
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a tiny-account drop stretching lead time and working capital with no queue leverage

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name off-paper and inverted-duty costs as mechanism / cash-cycle, never as a per-garment COGS add
anti_rework_rules.prevents: fabricating a per-unit figure for an episodic or working-capital cost
